newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST - Danish oil/gas seen 16.5 pct up in 1997.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Danish oil/gas seen 16.5 pct up in 1997.

text.p: Denmark's state energy agency on Wednesday forecast a rise in total 1997 oil and gas condensate production of 16.5 percent over 1996 and said production would be 26.4 percent higher in 2000 than last year.

It reported 1996 oil and gas production - virtually entirely derived from Danish North Sea offshore oil and gas rigs - of 12.09 million cubic metres or 10.29 million tonnes, estimating total 1997 production 12 percent higher at 14.1 million cubic metres.
In a statement the agency also forecast oil and gas production would rise to 15.3 million cubic metres in the year 2000, with Denmark self-sufficient in energy from this year onwards.

The figures were an upward adjustment of previous forecasts by 10-42 percent for the period, with the improved expectations based on high hopes of increased production from the new South Arne and Siri North Sea offshore fields, the agency said.
Maersk Oil & Gas, a unit of Danish A.P.Moeller, Norway's Statoil and Amerada Hess are leading operators in the Danish North Sea.
